geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing macro into a courtyard-forming macro to strengthen the public void and ground response.
Bound the courtyard proportion to keep the mass compact and occupiable.
Open the void toward the verified access edge to make the frontage legible.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant split-wing/cantilever into a clearer occupied court logic so the mass produces a legible public void rather than a generic break.
Keep the dominant longitudinal gesture while allowing the court to organize around the same primary bar axis.
Reduce the ambiguous reconnecting bridge effect so the void reads as intentional public space instead of a collision artifact.
Open the split more clearly to create a readable access seam and public threshold at ground level.
Size the court to remain occupiable and legible, not merely decorative subtraction.
Align the court opening to the verified access side so the public void responds to the frontage rather than turning away from it.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent single mass in most views, but the geometry is still unstable across projections: the stepped/bent body is legible, yet the public edge is weak and the carve does not convincingly resolve into an occupied court or entry seam. The form also feels more like a split, folded object than a compact neighborhood living bar with an active ground threshold. It partly resonates with the terraced/courtyard references, but it does not yet deliver their clear public void or grounded frontage response. Because the program demands a legible active edge and one clear public void or terrace, this fails hard-pass even though the overall massing is not chaotic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Larger campus-like spread and more articulated circulation than this compact bar; transfer the courtyard/terrace logic, not the breadth.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise, terraced, community-oriented massing with a carved central void and connected wings can support a neighborhood program while preserving a legible public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is flatter and more single-volume than the candidate; useful for ground response, not for the candidate’s stepped roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact pavilion-like street-building can use a simple upper mass with a clear entry setback/canopy to strengthen frontage and public legibility.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual reference; it is much more sweeping and residential/sectional than the candidate. Use only the sectional lesson, not the broad horseshoe form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced sectional massing can be transferred as a way to create inhabitable open space and continuous upper hierarchy.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied in the provided views, but the access response remains semantically weak relative to the marked frontage.
The blue frontage edge is not met by a clearly public undercut, court, or entry seam; the ground condition reads more sealed than activated.
Do not over-credit the stepped roof as program fit; the section still needs a clearer neighborhood-appropriate public/ground relationship.
